transcript:
Meeting header:
15:00 UTC, 2027-03-12 | Duration ~46m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Mark (Veridian CTO), Sana (Eng Lead), Ethan (ML Eng), Rita (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to scope embeddings + reranking pilot; focus on throughput and vector DB integration.

00:00 Alex: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood inference, i have Priya and Luis with me, we'll do a short intro then dig into your architecture and goals
00:08 Mark: yeah thanks Alex, i'm Mark, CTO at Veridian, we build a large enterprise search product for energy analytics, uh main thing we're trying to solve is relevancy at scale
00:18 Priya: great, can you talk through current stack and where embeddings fit in today?
00:23 Sana: sure, so today we do a BM25 baseline in Elastic for recall, then a vector rerank step using Pinecone for approximate nearest neighbors and a small cross-encoder for final scoring. It's a bit brittle as we scale; we see tail latency spikes when traffic hits 150-200 qps and cost of the cross-encoder is high
00:41 Luis: got it. are you embedding on the fly or precomputing?
00:45 Ethan: precompute for docs, real-time for queries. Our doc embed dim is 1536 (openai style) and queries are 1536 as well. Index size is about 100k docs per core product, but some customers have 1M+ docs
01:02 Alex: okay that clarifies. target qps you're describing 150-200, what's the 99p latency SLO for search?
01:08 Mark: I would say 200 ms for user-facing search, 500ms for internal dashboards is fine; the cross-encoder makes it hard to keep under 200 when query load rises
01:18 Priya: when you say cross-encoder, is that a BERT-like model hosted yourself? what size?
01:23 Sana: it's a medium cross-encoder, like a small BERT 6-layer fine-tuned model, about 120M params, and it runs on an inference fleet today
01:31 Alex: cool. we often see two approaches: push as much into ANN rerank to avoid heavy cross-encoder calls, or use a small candidate set and do targeted cross-encoder rerank. For Redwood we can help with both - optimize embedding model + serve reranker as low-latency endpoint or recommend dedicated infra.
01:47 Mark: could you explain Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in the context of vector workloads? we need to know isolation and network setup for Pinecone etc
01:56 Priya: sure. Hosted is our managed API - easiest to start, model catalog included, but shared pool. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools that you control for predictable throughput and we can colocate the reranker and embedder to minimize network hops. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you a customer-owned control plane with VPC peering, no data leaves your network by default and you manage keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For vector DB integration we support pushing embeddings into external services (Pinecone, Milvus) or hosting nearest neighbor with our runtime + FAISS/HNSW-backed indexes on Dedicated or Private if you want everything in your VPC.
02:29 Mark: are there customers who host both embeddings in Pinecone and use Redwood for reranking?
02:33 Priya: yes, mixed setups are common. For example Pinecone for indexing at scale, Redwood for embedding + cross-encoder rerank. We can also optionally host the ANN index in the Dedicated pool to reduce inter-service network latency.
02:43 Ethan: on the embedding model side, do you recommend 1536 vs 768? We're currently on 1536 and storage/cost is starting to bite
02:51 Luis: tradeoffs: higher dimension typically yields better semantic resolution but costs more in storage and ANN compute. For many workloads 768 or even 384 can be adequate if the model is tuned; another lever is quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) and index compression. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles based on your workload to hit cost targets
03:12 Sana: hybrid search question - how should we combine BM25 score with embedding similarity? we currently do a linear combination but want to understand best practice for reranking
03:20 Priya: common pattern: retrieve with BM25 to get high recall, then do ANN on embedding for semantic candidates, merge candidate lists and normalize scores, then cross-encoder rerank top-K. The exact weighting depends on query distribution, we recommend running an A/B over a production-like prompt set. Redwood's eval tooling can help automate that and detect regressions.
03:47 Mark: we use Pinecone now but some teams prefer an open source vector DB (Milvus/Weaviate/Chroma) for cost reasons. Does Redwood integrate with them?
03:55 Alex: yes we have connectors and customer stories for Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, Chroma, and for teams that want maximum control we run FAISS/HNSW inside Dedicated or Private. The integration choices affect latency: external service calls add network hop which can increase 99p by 10-50ms depending on region and peering.
04:13 Ethan: can you give rough numbers for embedding throughput per GPU on Redwood Dedicated? like how many qps can a single GPU serve for 1536-dim embeddings and a small cross-encoder rerank?
04:23 Priya: ballpark: an A100-class GPU with optimized kernels and batching can do ~600-1200 embedding inferences per second for small embed models with batching, but real-world numbers depend on batch sizes and sequence lengths. For cross-encoder rerank it's heavier - a 100-300 qps range per GPU depending on model size and use of quantization/optimizations. We can run benchmarks with your dataset to get realistic numbers
04:45 Mark: okay that aligns. our concerns are tail latency and cost; if we commit to Dedicated what's the typical procurement/lead time?
04:51 Alex: Dedicated trial can be spun up in days for small reserved pools; enterprise procurement for larger reserved capacity typically takes weeks but we support POs and contract terms. For Private/VPC there is an onboarding project which can be 2-6 weeks depending on network and security reviews.
05:05 Rita: on security, do you support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and customer-managed keys? we need SOC2 and any FedRAMP?
05:13 Priya: yes SSO/SAML, granular RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM) are available for Dedicated and Private. We have a SOC2 report and can share it under NDA. FedRAMP is not standard but we can discuss partner options for gov clouds.
05:29 Mark: good - please send SOC2 and encryption docs
05:32 Alex: will do.
05:34 Sana: about hybrid reranking, what's the recommended top-K for candidate generation before cross-encoder? 100? 50?
05:40 Priya: typical is 100 to 500 for ANN and then rerank top 10-50 with cross-encoder. That depends on recall needs and cost tolerance. We've seen diminishing returns after 200 for many enterprise search cases.
05:55 Ethan: what's the implication for vector index RAM? for 100k docs at 1536 dim with float32 that's substantial, but we use quantized indexes - curious what you'd recommend for Dedicated hosting
06:06 Luis: with HNSW and PQ or product quantization and 8-bit/4-bit quantization you can cut RAM by 4-8x. Also embedding float32 -> float16 helps storage and compute. We'll provide recommendations tailored to your index size in the benchmark repo.
06:20 Mark: how do you handle model upgrades and rollouts? we need canarying and safe rollback for rerankers
06:27 Alex: Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin model versions for production and set gradual rollouts with traffic slices. We also integrate quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions quickly.
06:40 Sana: for metrics we'd want token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns, does that show up?
06:44 Luis: yes Console shows per-route/model dashboards with token and request-level breakdowns, plus tracing hooks and error analysis.
06:50 Mark: let's get into the benchmark plan - what would you need from us to run a realistic load test?
06:55 Priya: sample dataset (10k-100k docs), query logs with 10k queries that represent distribution, success criteria (99p latency target, throughput qps, relevance metrics like MRR/NDCG), and access to an S3 bucket or we can provide a secure upload link. We'll spin up a Dedicated trial, run both Hosted and Dedicated comparisons, run ANN configs (HNSW/IVF/PQ) and record cost estimates
07:24 Mark: we can do that, we'll aim to provide a 10k subset this week.
07:28 Alex: perfect. one practical note: if you're using external Pinecone we often suggest colocating Redwood Dedicated in same cloud region and enabling VPC peering to reduce latency; for Private we can run everything inside your VPC so no external hops
07:44 Ethan: any gotchas with dimensionality and indexing? we've seen high-dim spaces degrade ANN quality sometimes
07:50 Priya: yes high-dim can make ANN less efficient; we sometimes do PCA or model distillation to smaller dims, or use specialized ANN indexes tuned for high-dim. Also distance metric matters - cosine vs dot product - make sure your ANN implementation and ranker are aligned.
08:07 Mark: pricing question - if we commit to Dedicated reserved capacity, how flexible is bursting? some months traffic spikes 3x
08:14 Alex: Dedicated has burst capacity options; you rent a baseline reserved pool and allow burst on demand with pay-as-you-go pricing. Auto-scaling policies configurable. We'll include burst and overage examples in the pricing sheet.
08:28 Sana: on data residency, we have EU customers who require all data to stay in EU. Does Redwood support region pinning?
08:34 Luis: yes, region pinning and control plane options for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have EU regions, but some legal teams still prefer Private deployments with on-prem or VPC-only egress controls.
08:44 Mark: sounds good. could we talk about reranking architecture - do you recommend reranker as a separate microservice or co-located with the ANN index?
08:52 Priya: co-locating reduces network latency; if cost is a concern you can separate them and only call the reranker for top candidates. Some customers run a lightweight reranker on CPU for small models and only call GPU reranker for heavy models. Redwood supports deploying rerankers in the Dedicated pool so you can choose layout.
09:12 Ethan: anything special for monitoring and traces per-query? we need to tie drops in NDCG to code changes
09:18 Luis: Redwood Console tracing hooks allow per-request traces and link to prompt/eval sets; we can emit flags when model score distributions shift and set regression alerts. You can also push logs to your SIEM.
09:30 Mark: ok let's recap next steps
09:33 Alex: recap: we will send pricing + SOC2 + kms/encryption doc; Priya will schedule a one-week Dedicated benchmark with the sample dataset; Veridian will provide dataset and query logs; we'll run comparisons against your Pinecone baseline and report metrics and cost estimates.
09:50 Sana: good, timeline: aim to start benchmark by 2027-03-20 if we get data by 03-15
09:56 Alex: sounds good, we'll follow up with calendar invite and next steps doc. Thanks everyone.

(End of transcript)
